nodes.summary: For every covariant derivative $\nabla$ on a vector bundle $V$ over a manifold $M$, every $x \in M$, all $u, v \in T_x M$ and every $\sigma \in V_x$, the curvature expression $R$ of $\nabla$ on extensions satisfies $R(u, v)\sigma = -R(v, u)\sigma$.
nodes.title: Antisymmetry of the curvature expression

nodes.summary: Let $\nabla$ be a covariant derivative on a vector bundle $V$ over a manifold $M$, let $x \in M$, let $u, v \in T_x M$ and let $\sigma \in V_x$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be the vector fields on $M$ whose coordinates in the preferred local trivialization of $TM$ at $x$ are constant, equal to those of $u$ and $v$, on the base set of that trivialization, with a fixed but unspecified value at each point outside it; let $S$ be…
nodes.title: Curvature expression of a covariant derivative on extensions

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself, so that each tangent space of $F$ is $F$. For every point $x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point $y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$) has value $u$ at $y$.
nodes.title: Extending a tangent vector of a normed space gives a constant vector field

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional normed space over a nontrivially normed field $\mathbb{K}$, let $\nabla$ be a covariant derivative on the tangent bundle of $M$, let $R$ be its curvature expression on extensions, let $x \in M$ and let $v, w \in T_x M$. With $e_1, \dots, e_n$ the fixed basis of $T_x M$ chosen for every finite-dimensional space and $e_1^*, \dots, e_n^*$ its coordinate…
nodes.title: Ricci contraction of the curvature expression

nodes.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ is Einstein when there is a real constant $\lambda$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, w) = \lambda \, g_x(v, w)$ for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature ([Lang], Einstein manifolds). Ricci-flat is the case $\lambda = 0$.
nodes.title: Einstein metric

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space, and let $\nabla$ be its Levi-Civita connection. For every point $x \in F$ and tangent vector $w \in T_xF$, let $W$ be the extension of $w$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$; it is the constant vector field with value $w$). Then the…
nodes.title: The Levi-Civita connection of Euclidean space kills constant vector fields

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For every point $x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point $y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$), viewed as a map from $F$ to its tangent bundle, is differentiable at $y$, not only at the base point $x$.
nodes.title: Extensions of tangent vectors of a normed space are differentiable

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For points $x, x' \in F$ and tangent vectors $a \in T_xF$ and $b \in T_{x'}F$, let $X$ and $Y$ be the extensions of $a$ and $b$ to vector fields on $F$ (built from the trivializations of the tangent bundle at $x$ and at $x'$). Then the Lie bracket $[X, Y]$ vanishes at every point $y \in F$.
nodes.title: Lie brackets of extended tangent vectors of a normed space vanish

nodes.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ has Ricci curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$, written $\operatorname{Ric} \ge k g$, when $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, v) \ge k \|v\|^2$ for every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature and $\|v\|$ is the norm of $v$ given by $g$.
nodes.title: Ricci curvature bounded below

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_xF$, the Ricci curvature $\mathrm{Ric}(v, w)$ of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Euclidean space is Ricci-flat

nodes.summary: For a point $x$ of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ and tangent vectors $v, w \in T_x M$, the Ricci curvature is $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, w) = \sum_i e_i^*(R(e_i, v) w)$, where $R$ is the Riemann curvature endomorphism of the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, $(e_i)$ is a fixed basis of $T_x M$ and $(e_i^*)$ is its dual basis; the contraction itself uses no metric. Since $z \mapsto R(z, v) w$ is linear, this…
nodes.title: Ricci curvature

nodes.summary: Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold. Its Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ is antisymmetric in its first two arguments: $R(u, v) w = -R(v, u) w$ for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_x M$.
nodes.title: Antisymmetry of the Riemann curvature

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_xF$, the Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ of $F$ at $x$ satisfies $R(u, v)w = 0$.
nodes.title: Euclidean space is flat

nodes.title: Riemann curvature endomorphism

nodes.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has scalar curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when its scalar curvature at every point $x \in M$ is at least $k$.
nodes.title: Scalar curvature bounded below

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$, the scalar curvature of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Euclidean space has zero scalar curvature

nodes.summary: The scalar curvature of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ at a point $x$ is $\sum_i \operatorname{Ric}_x(e_i, e_i)$, the metric trace of the Ricci curvature $\operatorname{Ric}$, where $(e_i)$ is a fixed orthonormal basis of $T_x M$ ([Gud, Def. 8.32]). The unit $n$-sphere has scalar curvature $n (n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Scalar curvature

nodes.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \ge k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Sectional curvature bounded below

nodes.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional curvature at most $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \le k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Sectional curvature bounded above

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ and every tangent vector $u \in T_x M$, the sectional curvature formula $K$ gives $K(u, u) = 0$: its denominator $\|u\|^2 \|u\|^2 - \langle u, u \rangle^2$ vanishes, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and $\|\cdot\|$ are the inner product and norm on $T_x M$ given by $g$, and a quotient by $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on equal vectors

nodes.summary: Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real space (boundary and corners allowed), and let $x \in M$, $u \in T_x M$ and $c \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the sectional curvature at $x$ satisfies $K(u, cu) = 0$: the denominator $\|u\|^2 \|cu\|^2 - \langle u, cu \rangle^2$ of its defining formula vanishes, and the quotient is then $0$ by definition.
nodes.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on a vector and a multiple of it

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xF$, the sectional curvature $K(u, v)$ of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Euclidean space has zero sectional curvature

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
